findings.summary: A partially unknown quota window remains routable
findings.detail: Admission is suspended only when every bucket is unknown (line 284), while routability requires merely one applicable numeric bucket. Sequence: a provider reports rolling-5h=60 and weekly=null, both covering `cto`; `enrich` returns OPEN and `isRoutableFor` returns true. Continuity can then assign and fail over to a provider whose limiting weekly quota is UNKNOWN, violating §14.3, CP-S16/CP-S17, and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Evaluate every quota window applicable to the requested capability. Any unknown applicable limiting bucket must make that capability non-routable; only unrelated buckets may be ignored.

findings.summary: Dispatch admission can use an unrelated healthy provider to bypass a failed target provider
findings.detail: `refreshForDispatch` allows dispatch when any production provider is not SUSPENDED; it receives neither the selected provider nor required capabilities. Sequence: an existing PRIMARY_CTO is bound to Claude, Claude's capacity probe fails, GPT is OPEN, `refreshForDispatch` allows because of GPT, and dispatch reuses the READY Claude binding. New work is therefore allocated to the provider whose probe failed, contradicting §14.3, CP-S17, and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Perform admission against the exact target binding/provider and required capability after target selection. A failed target-provider probe must block that allocation regardless of other providers.

findings.summary: Mandatory refresh triggers are declarations rather than enforced paths
findings.detail: Repository call sites never use `BLIND_REVIEW` or `PROVIDER_SWITCH_OR_FAILURE` in production, and `WORKER_FANOUT` is refreshed only when a caller explicitly requests it through `capacity_get`. A mandatory blind review currently probes runtime and starts a session without capacity refresh. This omits three refresh obligations from §14.2.
findings.suggestedFix: Add mandatory capacity gates directly to blind-review constitution, large fan-out admission, and provider switch/allocation-failure handling. Do not make these refreshes caller-optional.

findings.summary: Dynamic reserve omits required inputs and has no effect on production admission
findings.detail: The reserve accepts only invocation/review/run counts; it ignores reset time and burn rate required by §14.5. It also treats an unknown bucket as 100% headroom at line 229. No production routing or admission path consumes this function, while `refreshForDispatch` admits CONSERVE providers without applying role priority or reserve.
findings.suggestedFix: Compute reserve from applicable buckets, reset horizon, measured burn rate, in-flight work, expected reviews, and role demand; fail closed on unknown inputs and enforce the result in allocation routing.

findings.summary: Future-dated observations are accepted as indefinitely fresh evidence
findings.detail: A future `observedAt` produces a negative age and is classified HEALTHY. `CapacityMonitor.enrich` then clamps that age to zero. A stale capacity file dated far in the future will consequently remain OPEN and dominate stored snapshots until that date, bypassing the configurable freshness window and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Reject observations beyond a small configured clock-skew allowance and normalize accepted timestamps before persistence.

findings.summary: The runtime probe cannot verify an existing critical session
findings.detail: The interface described as a liveness check takes no session identity. Both CLI implementations merely run `<binary> --version`. That succeeds while authentication, network access, the provider service, or the existing critical session is unusable. A missing quota file can therefore yield sensor ERROR but runtime HEALTHY without the separate session-health evidence required by §14.3 and CP-S17.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a session-aware health probe and perform an authenticated provider operation or session-specific no-op. Preserve UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE when actual provider or session liveness cannot be demonstrated.

findings.summary: Agent CLI processes inherit daemon credentials and filesystem authority
findings.detail: `runCli` spawns every role process under the daemon identity with the complete `process.env` and no filesystem boundary around control-plane state. A non-read-only Claude CTO invocation can therefore inherit `GH_TOKEN` or connector secrets and can read the default daemon-only secret store or rewrite structured capacity files. Unix mode 0700 does not isolate children running as the same user. This violates CP-HI-05 and the prohibition on exposing trusted GitHub authority credentials to agent sessions.
findings.suggestedFix: Run agent CLIs under a separately confined identity/container, use an explicit environment allowlist, strip GitHub/Buzz/Telegram authority variables, and deny read/write access to the database, secret store, and capacity-source directories.

findings.summary: A non-production adapter can replace a production provider and enter continuity coverage
findings.detail: `register` silently overwrites adapters by provider ID and performs no production check. `ScriptedAdapter` permits an arbitrary provider ID while advertising fabricated healthy capacity, and `ContinuityKernel` builds candidates from `providers.list()` rather than `production()`. Sequence: register `ScriptedAdapter(clock, "gpt")` after boot, exhaust real providers, evaluate coverage, then fail over; the scripted adapter can be reported as FULL_COVERAGE and receive a critical role.
findings.suggestedFix: Reject duplicate provider IDs and non-production adapters in the runtime registry used by production. Continuity, blind review, and failover must independently require `isProduction` before counting or binding an adapter.

findings.summary: Continuity freshness and mode changes are not atomic
findings.detail: `evaluated_at` is committed before the separate mode update. Sequence: state is NORMAL, evaluation computes SURVIVAL, the freshness update commits, and the process crashes before line 234. After restart, `assertCompletionAllowed` sees a fresh NORMAL mode and permits production completion for up to five minutes despite no valid coverage, violating §15.6 and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Update mode, reason, changed time, evaluated time, and the authoritative transition audit in one database transaction.

findings.summary: Failover self-certifies a fabricated session as READY and permits a missing route
findings.detail: Both production `startSession` methods only return a random UUID; they do not create or contact a provider session. Failover immediately marks that record READY, then invokes a readiness port which in the default wiring only rereads this lifecycle value. Buzz connection is optional, and production wiring does not attach it to the continuity kernel. The binding can therefore switch to a session with neither demonstrated provider readiness nor a logical route, contrary to §15.7 and CP-HI-08.
findings.suggestedFix: Create or authenticate the real provider session first, require successful logical-route connection, run an independent readiness probe, and transition to READY only after both succeed. Refuse failover when either port is absent.

findings.summary: Active workers are omitted from coverage planning and cannot be failed over
findings.detail: `requiredRoles` includes only CEO, project CTOs, and blind reviewers. It never inspects active WORKER bindings or task executions. The failover scope also lacks `taskId`, so a worker binding cannot be switched even if requested. A provider outage during active worker execution can still produce FULL_COVERAGE while the active role is uncovered, contrary to §15.3 and the PRD requirement that Worker runtimes be failover-capable.
findings.suggestedFix: Include every active scoped role, including worker/task bindings and executions, in the plan; add task scope and the worker model path to failover.

findings.summary: Restoration reports success without restoring any binding
findings.detail: For an eligible fallback role, `restore` only appends the role key to `restored`; it never creates a preferred session or calls `bindings.switchTo`. Sequence: a fallback CTO has no active runs, its preferred provider recovers, `restore()` returns the CTO in `restored`, but the active binding remains FALLBACK. This is a false success report forbidden by CP-HI-08 and does not implement §15.8.
findings.suggestedFix: Perform preferred-session creation, routing, readiness, and atomic binding switch before adding a role to `restored`; otherwise return it as deferred or merely eligible.

findings.summary: Capacity snapshot replacement is not atomic
findings.detail: The delete and per-bucket inserts are separate autocommit statements despite the comment claiming one atomic observation. A crash, disk error, or invalid later bucket after the delete/first insert leaves a partial multi-window snapshot. `current()` can then route using the surviving healthy window while the missing limiting window is silently absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap deletion and all bucket inserts for one observation in `db.tx`; rollback the entire replacement on any failure.
